text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: elevated 5xx rate detected on private-gw-prod (us-west-2) - gateway-504-rate > 5% over 5m. Paging SRE oncall. Correlation: NAT/egress metrics spike, conntrack usage rising.

maria: acked, jumping in. seeing ~12% 504s on loadbalancer -> private-gw-prod. Routing looks healthy but SNAT source port exhaustion trending up.

josh: confirmed, dashboards show ephemeral_port_usage ~98% on nat-01 and nat-02. traffic pattern spike from batch inference jobs.

vikram: tagging net-eng, could be peering route multipath + asymmetric SNAT churn causing return-path drops. @net-eng can you confirm any peering flaps?

net-eng: looking now, BGP near flapping on peering-peer-12 around 15:03: see intermittent withdraws -> reannounce. No planned changes.

maria: quick impact note for CS: we have increased 5xx for customers using private VPC inference gateway; estimated affected requests ~4-7% total, some customers hitting timeouts. @customer-success - heads up.

customer-success: notified top-3 affected customers, they're seeing 504s. one reported degraded UX on inference endpoints. escalation ready if needed.

sre-oncall: triage checklist: 1) verify conntrack & ephemeral port exhaustion 2) check NAT metric heatmaps 3) check SG/route changes 4) apply mitigation: enlarge ephemeral range or rotate NATs 5) fallback to public gateway if sustained. proceeding.

josh: pulling conntrack counters on nat-01: `conntrack -S` shows entries close to limit. running `ss` shows many TIME_WAIT. suspect clients not reusing connections because of many distinct src ports exhausted.

maria: running quick tcpdump on gateway to confirm retransmits: `tcpdump -i eth0 'tcp port 443 and (tcp[tcpflags] & tcp-syn) != 0'` - seeing SYNs from backend but responses not reaching client intermittently.

net-eng: peering logs: `bgp-monitor` shows short withdraws at 15:02:47, 15:03:05, 15:03:22 - route convergence holding but multipath changed. I think with high ephemeral usage, the NAT device struggled to maintain sessions during small route churn leading to 504s.

vikram: mitigation proposal: 1) temporarily increase SNAT ephemeral port pool on nat instances (apply sysctl net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range) 2) add a short-lived secondary NAT path by bringing up nat-03 in same AZ 3) throttle noisy batch inference jobs via token bucket at edge. I'll script ephemeral range change.

maria: while you do that I'll add a canary routing policy to divert 10% of private-gw-prod traffic to nat-03 when it's ready.

josh: running command to expand local port range on nat-01 (example):
```
echo "1024 65535" > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=2000000
```
Applied on nat-01 and nat-02, restarting `conntrack` service to pick up changes.

net-eng: provisioning nat-03 now, attaching to same private subnet, will advertise via peering once ready.

incident-bot: Deploy bot: rolling instance config change applied to nat-01 and nat-02 by josh at 15:07:21.

maria: after port-range bump + conntrack increase we see ephemeral_port_usage drop to ~72% and 5xx rate trending down to 2.6% within 90s. Nice.

customer-success: relaying improvement to customers, one reported recoveries on their end.

vikram: nat-03 is up, peering learned new path. I applied temporary route-map to prefer nat-03 for a small subset. Monitoring for asymmetric flows.

josh: quick check: `iptables -t nat -L -n` looks unchanged. Security groups haven't been modified in last 24h per audit logs. Not root-cause but contributed.

maria: logs show a burst of short-lived connections from batch-infer cluster that correlated with top talkers. We should throttle or add connection pooling on clients.

net-eng: BGP watchers show no further withdraws since 15:09:10. peering stabilization confirmed.

sre-oncall: current status: incident mitigated -> 5xx < 1% for last 5m, ephemeral usage stable, nat-03 holding traffic. Moving to monitor.

vikram: follow-up actions (owner): 1) permanent increase of conntrack/port config (net-eng) 2) implement backpressure for batch-infer (product/infra) 3) runbook update: add quick steps for ephemeral expansion + bringup nat-03 (maria) 4) root-cause postmortem if recurrence (sre-oncall).

maria: I'll draft runbook snippet now and assign to PR.

customer-success: customers updated, no escalations for now.

josh: logging note - save tcpdump slices and conntrack dumps to s3://redwood-incident-dumps/2445678901/ for post-incident analysis.

incident-bot: Incident transitioned to MONITORING by maria at 15:15:55.

sre-oncall: handing to dayteam in 30m. leaving runbook pointers in the thread. Please escalate if 5xx rises again. :thumbsup:

maria: adding links and commands used to the runbook: 
- `aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=nat-*`
- `conntrack -L --timeout`
- `sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range='1024 65535'`
- `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=2000000`
- `tcpdump -w /tmp/gw-syn-sample.pcap 'tcp port 443 and tcp[tcpflags] & tcp-syn != 0'`

vikram: post-incident follow-ups: schedule peering debug with cloud provider, check for MTU/ECMP edge cases, and add metric alarm on ephemeral_port_usage > 85% to preempt.

maria: thanks team. closing active paging loop, keeping thread open for follow-ups.

sre-oncall: last check at 15:29:15 - healthy.

net-eng: added note in ops-ticket OPS-5239 to track BGP watcher tuning.

customer-success: closing customer updates, will reopen if any regression. :white_check_mark:
